...using a board and stick, they just stood there; I do not know what they used, but they beat him soundly, breaking the skin in two places on his face. We heard that the aunt has a kind of ointment here for cane wounds. Could you, Miss, find a pill for me?

Baochai listened, then hurriedly ordered Ying'er to find two pills to give to Ping'er. Baochai said, "Since that is the case, you go and convey my greetings; I will not go myself." Ping'er responded to Baochai and left. That is all for now.

Now, after Xiangling had met with everyone and finished her evening meal, Baochai and the others went to Grandmother Jia's quarters, so she went to the Xiaoxiang Lodge. By this time, Daiyu had largely recovered, and she was naturally delighted to see that Xiangling had also moved into the garden to live. Xiangling smiled and said, "Now that I have finally moved in and have some free time, if you could teach me how to write poetry, it would be my great fortune!" Daiyu smiled and said, "If you want to learn poetry, you must take me as your teacher. Although I am not an expert, I can certainly teach you the basics." Xiangling laughed, "If you truly mean that, I will take you as my teacher, but you must not get tired of me." Daiyu said, "What is so difficult that it requires great effort to learn? It is nothing more than the <term>qichengzhuanhe</term> <gloss>introduction, development, transition, and conclusion</gloss>. The middle part, the development and transition, consists of two pairs of lines. The tones should be contrasted: level tones against oblique tones, abstract concepts against concrete images, and concrete images against abstract concepts. If you happen to write a truly exceptional line, it is perfectly acceptable even if the tonal patterns or the abstract-concrete balance are not strictly followed."

Xiangling smiled and said, "No wonder that when I occasionally read an old poem, I see some that are crafted with extreme precision and others that are not. I also heard the saying, 'The first, third, and fifth characters do not matter; the second, fourth, and sixth must be distinct.' Yet, when I look at the poems of the ancients, some follow this, while others have the second, fourth, and sixth characters wrong. That is why I have been confused every day. Now that I have heard what you said, it seems these rules are not so rigid after all, and the most important thing is that the phrasing and imagery should be fresh and unique." Daiyu said, "That is exactly the principle. Phrasing and vocabulary are, in the end, secondary; the first priority is to have a clear concept. If the sentiment and intent are genuine, even without polished phrasing, the poem will naturally be good. This is what is called 'not letting the words harm the meaning.'"

Xiangling said, "I only love Lu Fangweng's lines, 'The heavy curtains are not rolled up, the fragrance lingers long; the ancient inkstone is slightly worn, holding much ink.' They are truly vivid and interesting!" Daiyu said, "You absolutely must not read poetry like that. Because you do not yet know poetry, you love it when you see something shallow and accessible. Once you fall into that style, you will never be able to learn properly. Just listen to me: if you truly want to learn, I have the <term>Wang Mojie Quanji</term> <gloss>Complete Works of Wang Wei</gloss> here. You should carefully study his hundred five-character regulated verses until you have mastered them. Then, read the hundred and twenty seven-character regulated verses of Old Du <note>Du Fu</note>, and after that, read one or two hundred of Li Qinglian's <note>Li Bai</note> seven-character quatrains. Once you have built a foundation with these three in your mind, you can look at the works of Tao Yuanming, Ying, Liu, Xie, Ruan, Yu, and Bao. You are a person of such extreme intelligence; it will not take a year before you become a true poet!" Xiangling heard this, smiled, and said, "In that case, dear Miss, please get that book for me. I will take it back and read a few pieces at night." Daiyu heard this and ordered Zijian to bring the five-character regulated verses of Wang Youcheng <note>Wang Wei</note> and handed them to Xiangling, saying, "Only read the ones with red circles; they are the ones I have selected. Read them one by one. If there is anything you do not understand, ask your young mistress; or, if you happen to meet me, I will explain it to you."

Xiangling took the poems and returned to the Hengwu Court. Neglecting everything else, she read them one by one under the lamp. Baochai urged her several times to go to sleep, but she would not. Seeing her such devotion, Baochai had no choice but to let her be.

One day, just after Daiyu had finished washing and combing, she saw Xiangling come in, smiling, to return the book, wanting to exchange it for the regulated verses of Du <note>Du Fu</note>. Daiyu smiled and asked, "How many have you memorized in total?" Xiangling smiled and said, "I have finished reading all the ones with red circles." Daiyu asked, "Have you gained any understanding from them?" Xiangling smiled and said, "I think I have gained some understanding, though I am not sure if it is correct. Let me tell you what I think."

<summary>Daiyu instructs Xiangling on the fundamentals of poetry and provides her with a curriculum of classical masters for study.</summary>
<keywords>Daiyu, Xiangling, Baochai, Poetry, Wang Wei, Du Fu, Literary Education</keywords>
